children: Euronext wheat extended gains on Wednesday to post more contract highs, with traders seeing little sign of de-escalation of hostilities in the Black Sea region to alleviate a near-halt to Russian and Ukrainian shipments there.
Firm prices for crude oil and corn also supported buying in wheat, traders said.
on Euronext was up 1.3% at €256.75 ($297.57) a metric ton by 1705 GMT.
It earlier reached €259.25, surpassing a previous life-of-contract peak from Tuesday to set a two-year high for a second-month price
Attacks in recent weeks brought grain loadings at Russian and Ukrainian Black Sea ports to a virtual halt, increasing pressure on importers to seek alternatives.

Hopes of de-escalation, nurtured by Turkish efforts to broker safe passage for grain trade, have been dampened by Russia's rejection of a grain deal and continued attacks by Moscow and Kyiv on each other's ports and shipping.
"Nothing has changed on the ground; it's worse even," one futures trader said.
Russian forces struck two cargo vessels on Wednesday, one in Ukraine's port of Chornomorsk and another in the Black Sea, Russia's Defence Ministry said.
confirmed that its terminal in Odesa, another Ukrainian Black Sea port, was damaged on Monday during an attack.
The squeeze on Russian and Ukrainian exports has shifted some demand towards EU origins, though weather-hit grain harvests could limit availability in Europe.
In Germany, the 2026 all-wheat crop has fallen 10.1% on the year to 20.81 million tons after this summer’s heatwave and drought, the agriculture ministry said on Wednesday.

“The figures were expected after similar earlier forecasts by farming associations but are certainly disappointing ... in view of hopes Germany could win more exports if Russian and Ukrainian shipments remain disrupted,” a German trader said.
In France, a warm, dry spell this week has revived concerns about parched conditions for planting after record heat and drought.
Farming losses are expected to trim overall French growth this year, the finance ministry said. Farmers are awaiting a government aid package that has been delayed.
Financial investors expanded their net long position in Euronext wheat last week, data from the exchange showed.
